answer.location_description: Whole image: a horizontal stripe or grating pattern repeating every 4 rows. Rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 are bright; rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23 are dark. It spans all columns.
answer.shortcut_type: periodic horizontal stripe pattern (scan-line / grating artifact)
answer.mechanism: Layer-1 units 8, 9, 10, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 29 are stripe detectors in phase A: they weight bright rows {0,1,4,5,8,9,...} positively and the rows in between negatively. Their row weights roughly cancel on a uniform image, so they fire only for this grating. Their large negative biases (about -61 to -97) make them selective. They feed layer-2 units u3, u4, u10, u12 and u13 with large positive weights, and those units have positive output weights (+63, +77, +67, +42, +71). They also strongly suppress u1 and u7, which have the most negative output weights (-94, -99). Units 2, 3, 23 and 31 are opposite-phase detectors with large positive biases. They act as the 'no stripes' path: they feed u1 and u7 positively and inhibit u3, u4, u10, u12 and u13, which pushes toward benign.
answer.evidence: Unit 8 rows 0-1 are about +30, rows 2-3 about -30, rows 4-5 about +35, rows 6-7 about -40, and so on through row 23. Units 9, 10, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 29 show the same 2-on/2-off row pattern across all 24 columns. Units 2, 3, 23 and 31 show the inverted phase (e.g. unit 23 rows 2-3 about +40, rows 4-5 about -30). Layer-2 weights: u4 takes 63, 63, 74, 83, 93 and 59 from units 9, 10, 20, 24, 27 and 29. u13 takes 99, 63 and 75 from units 9, 24 and 27. u1 takes -73, -89, -66 and -68 from units 9, 20, 24 and 27. Output weights: u4 +77, u13 +71, u10 +67, u3 +63, u1 -94, u7 -99. Stripe-detector units 0, 4, 5, 6, 7, 11-17, 19, 21, 22, 25, 26, 28 and 30 have small random-looking weights and are essentially unused. No anatomical nodule property would produce a full-field 4-pixel horizontal grating.
answer.main_feature: Apart from the stripes, the same units carry a localized central pattern: strongly negative weights around rows 10-11, cols 16-18 and positive weights around rows 14-17, cols 10-12. This suggests some sensitivity to nodule intensity and shape near the image centre, but the dominant learned signal is the full-image horizontal stripe pattern.
